questions.stem:
A particle, P, of mass 0.5 kg is moving along the positive x-axis. At time t seconds, $t \geqslant 0$, P is x metres from the origin O and is moving away from O with velocity $v\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, where $v = \frac{1}{(4x+3)}$

When $t = 0$, P is at O.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the distance of P from O when $t = 2$
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
$v = \frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{1}{(4x+3)}$
$\frac{dt}{dx} = 4x+3$
$t = \int (4x+3)\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\times 4x^2+3x+c$
OR $\int_0^2 dt = \int_0^X (4x+3)\,dx = \left[\frac{1}{2}\times 4x^2+3x\right]_0^X$
M1,dM1A1: Rewrite as $\frac{dx}{dt}$ and separate variables to reach a form ready for integration (M1); attempt the integration (at least one power going up) (dM1); correct integration, constant/limits not needed (A1)
$c=0$
$t=2=\frac{1}{2}\times 4x^2+3x$, $2x^2+3x-2=0$ dM1: Use $t=2$ in their expression or substitute correct limits, and solve their 3 term quadratic to find $x$. If solving an incorrect quadratic, evidence of a correct method must be seen. Depends on the previous M mark.
$x=\frac{1}{2}$ ($x=-2$) A1cso: Obtain $x=\frac{1}{2}$ (and reject $-2$ if seen) from completely correct work. Constant of integration must have been seen, although we do not need to see evidence of evaluation.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the magnitude of the resultant force acting on P when $t = 2$
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
$a = v\frac{dv}{dx}$ alt: $a = \frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{1}{2}v^2\right)$ M1: Use $a = v\frac{dv}{dx}$
$=\frac{1}{4x+3}\times\frac{-4}{(4x+3)^2}$ dM1A1: Differentiate the given expression for $v$ and obtain an expression for $a$. We need to see a power of 2 (or a power of 3 if using $\frac{d}{dx}(\frac{1}{2}v^2)$). Depends on the previous M mark. (A1: Correct expression, any form.)
$|F| = \frac{1}{2}\times\frac{4}{(2+3)^3} = \frac{2}{125} = 0.016\,\mathrm{N}$ M1 A1cso: Use their acceleration in an equation of motion to obtain a value for $F$. Mass must be included and they must use their value of $x$. Independent, but must have found an expression for acceleration. A1cso: Correct magnitude of $F$. Correct solution only. Can be fraction or decimal. Must be positive.

parts.label: main
parts.technique: Circular motion (rotating disc, friction providing centripetal force)
parts.reason: This problem requires circular motion concepts (angular speed, centripetal acceleration/force) which are not mentioned in any P or M statement in the 9MA0 specification; only projectiles, SHM-free topics like moments/forces/kinematics in a straight line or plane (constant acceleration/vectors) are covered. Circular motion is absent from the spec statements, so this part is out.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Circular motion on the inside of a hemispherical bowl with a taut string (conical-pendulum-type problem, resolving forces to find tension)
parts.reason: Requires circular motion (angular speed, centripetal force equations) which no statement in the specification mentions. This is a core M3 topic absent from 9MA0.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Circular motion - condition on normal reaction (R ≥ 0) to find minimum angular speed
parts.reason: Depends on the circular-motion setup and result of part (a); circular motion is not covered by any statement, and this part also relies on the out-of-spec previous part.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Work-energy equation involving elastic potential energy (Hooke's law), friction and gravity, on an inclined plane
parts.reason: This requires an energy method combining GPE, EPE (elastic potential energy) and work done against friction; work-energy and elastic potential energy concepts are not mentioned in any P or M statement (the spec's mechanics content is restricted to forces/Newton's laws, kinematics and moments), so this is out.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Change in acceleration due to change of direction of friction, using result from part (a)
parts.reason: Depends on the coefficient of friction µ found in part (a) via the out-of-spec energy method, so this part is also out.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Energy equation for a particle on a string moving in a vertical circle (projectile constrained by a string)
parts.reason: This is circular motion combined with an energy method (GPE/KE) for a particle on a string; circular motion is not covered by any spec statement.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Circular motion tension equations combined with Newton's experimental law (coefficient of restitution) at impact with the ceiling
parts.reason: Requires circular motion (tension = mv^2/r type equations) and Newton's experimental law/restitution, neither of which appears in any spec statement.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Simple harmonic motion - deriving SHM equation from Hooke's law forces on an elastic spring
parts.reason: Simple harmonic motion (SHM) is not mentioned by any statement in the specification; it is a core M3 topic absent from 9MA0.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Period of SHM from angular frequency
parts.reason: Depends on the SHM model established in part (a), which is out of spec; SHM itself is not covered by any statement.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Amplitude of SHM from v_max = aω
parts.reason: Requires the SHM framework and formulae (v_max = aω), which are not covered by any spec statement.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Time in SHM oscillation for which displacement exceeds a given value, using x = a cos ωt
parts.reason: Requires SHM formulae and inverse trig manipulation specific to SHM, which is not covered by any spec statement.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.technique: Volume of solid of revolution found by integrating πy^2 with respect to x
parts.reason: The spec's integration statements (P8.3) mention area under a curve and area between curves, but volumes of revolution are not mentioned by any statement; this specific technique (rotating a region 360° about the x-axis to find volume) is absent from the specification.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.technique: Centre of mass of a solid of revolution found using ∫xy^2dx / ∫y^2dx
parts.reason: Centre of mass is explicitly listed as a named concept excluded per the rules (no statement mentions centre of mass), and it also depends on the out-of-spec volume of revolution from (a)(i).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Centre of mass of a composite solid using moments of mass about a point
parts.reason: Centre of mass is a named excluded concept not mentioned by any statement, and this part also relies on the out-of-spec result from (a).
